# Plugins and marketplaces

Where these methods are:

- `session.plugins` — `Session.plugins`, a `SessionPlugins`
- `igni.marketplaces` — `IgniClient.marketplaces`, a `IgniMarketplaces`

Every method here is generated from igni-core's RPC contract; its documentation is igni's own. The examples run inside an `async` function with `igni` an open `IgniClient` and `session` one of its sessions ([Quick start](/docs/sdk/igni-client/quick-start)).

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`session.plugins.contents()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/plugins#session-plugins-contents) | Show what an installed plugin contains. |
| [`session.plugins.install()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/plugins#session-plugins-install) | Install a plugin from a git repository or a marketplace. |
| [`session.plugins.list()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/plugins#session-plugins-list) | List the installed plugins. |
| [`session.plugins.preview()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/plugins#session-plugins-preview) | Show what a plugin contains without installing it. |
| [`session.plugins.remove()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/plugins#session-plugins-remove) | Uninstall a plugin. |
| [`session.plugins.set_enabled()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/plugins#session-plugins-set-enabled) | Switch an installed plugin on or off. |
| [`session.plugins.update()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/plugins#session-plugins-update) | Move an installed plugin to another commit. |
| [`igni.marketplaces.add()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/plugins#igni-marketplaces-add) | Add a plugin marketplace and read its catalogue. |
| [`igni.marketplaces.list()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/plugins#igni-marketplaces-list) | List the plugin marketplaces igni knows, with their catalogues. |
| [`igni.marketplaces.refresh()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/plugins#igni-marketplaces-refresh) | Fetch marketplaces' catalogues again. |
| [`igni.marketplaces.remove()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/plugins#igni-marketplaces-remove) | Forget a plugin marketplace. |

## session.plugins.contents()

Show what an installed plugin contains.

```python
async def contents(self, name: str) -> PluginContents
```

`name` is the installed plugin. Returns its folder and its
skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers and tools, with its README; or
`error` when no such plugin is installed.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required | Name of the installed plugin. |

**Returns** [`PluginContents`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/models-reference#plugincontents).

**How long** `io` — Reads or writes the project, the session's database or the disk; a few seconds at most.
The client waits up to 30 seconds.

**Access** [`client`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — any connection igni admitted.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `get_plugin_contents`, scope `session`, area `plugins`; igni answers with `rpc_response`.

**Example**

```python
contents = await session.plugins.contents("acme-review")
print(contents.skills, contents.agents)
```

## session.plugins.install()

Install a plugin from a git repository or a marketplace.

```python
async def install(self, ref: str, *, install_ref: str | None = None) -> InfoMessage
```

`ref` is a git URL or `@<marketplace>/<plugin>`; `install_ref`
the branch, tag or commit to check out (the marketplace's, or the
default branch, when absent). The plugin is active in this session
at once. Returns an `info` message, sent in place of an
`rpc_response`, whose text says what was installed — or why not:
git missing, an unknown marketplace entry, the organisation's
policy, a git error.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `install_ref` | `str \| None` | `None` | Branch, tag or commit to check out; when absent, the marketplace's choice or the default branch. |
| `ref` | `str` | required | A git URL, or `@<marketplace>/<plugin>` for a marketplace plugin. |

**Returns** [`InfoMessage`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/events-reference#infomessage).

**How long** `long` — Runs something that takes as long as it takes: a git clone, the agent, a shell command, a model summarising.
The client waits up to 600 seconds.

**Access** [`window`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — Through Fleet's gateway every connection stands as igni's window and makes this call. On the desktop only the app's own window does: a program — with the lockfile's token or an approver token — gets `AccessRefused`.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`AccessRefused`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#accessrefused) when this connection does not stand as `window` · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `install_plugin`, scope `session`, area `plugins`; igni answers with `message`.

**Example**

```python
info = await session.plugins.install("acme-review@acme")
print(info.text)
```

## session.plugins.list()

List the installed plugins.

```python
async def list(self) -> list[PluginInfo]
```

Takes no arguments. Returns each plugin's name, version,
description, where it came from, whether it is enabled (a plugin
the organisation manages always is), the commit it is pinned to,
and what it brings: skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers.

Takes no arguments.

**Returns** `list[`[`PluginInfo`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/models-reference#plugininfo)`]`.

**How long** `io` — Reads or writes the project, the session's database or the disk; a few seconds at most.
The client waits up to 30 seconds.

**Access** [`client`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — any connection igni admitted.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `get_plugin_details`, scope `session`, area `plugins`; igni answers with `rpc_response`.

**Example**

```python
for plugin_info in await session.plugins.list():
    print(plugin_info.name, plugin_info.description)
```

## session.plugins.preview()

Show what a plugin contains without installing it.

```python
async def preview(
    self,
    source: str,
    *,
    branch: str | None = None,
    subdir: str | None = None,
) -> PluginContents
```

`source` is the plugin's git URL (optionally followed by a
subfolder); `branch` the branch, tag or commit to read (the
default branch when absent); `subdir` the plugin's folder inside
the repository, which wins over one in `source`. The repository
is cloned to a temporary place. Returns the same shape as
`get_plugin_contents`, with `preview_source` naming what was
read; or `error` when the organisation's policy refuses the
source, git is missing, or the clone failed.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `branch` | `str \| None` | `None` | Branch, tag or commit to read; the default branch when absent. |
| `source` | `str` | required | The plugin's git URL, optionally followed by a folder inside the repository. |
| `subdir` | `str \| None` | `None` | The plugin's folder inside the repository; overrides one given in `source`. |

**Returns** [`PluginContents`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/models-reference#plugincontents).

**How long** `long` — Runs something that takes as long as it takes: a git clone, the agent, a shell command, a model summarising.
The client waits up to 600 seconds.

**Access** [`client`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — any connection igni admitted.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `preview_plugin`, scope `session`, area `plugins`; igni answers with `rpc_response`.

**Example**

```python
preview = await session.plugins.preview("https://github.com/acme/review-plugin", branch="main")
print(preview.name, preview.readme[:200])
```

## session.plugins.set_enabled()

Switch an installed plugin on or off.

```python
async def set_enabled(self, *, enabled: bool, name: str) -> InfoMessage
```

`name` is the installed plugin; `enabled` its new state. The
choice is saved and this session reloads its plugins. Returns an
`info` message, sent in place of an `rpc_response`, whose text
says what happened — including a refusal: no such plugin, or one
the organisation manages.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `bool` | required | The plugin's new state: `true` to switch it on. |
| `name` | `str` | required | Name of the installed plugin. |

**Returns** [`InfoMessage`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/events-reference#infomessage).

**How long** `io` — Reads or writes the project, the session's database or the disk; a few seconds at most.
The client waits up to 30 seconds.

**Access** [`window`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — Through Fleet's gateway every connection stands as igni's window and makes this call. On the desktop only the app's own window does: a program — with the lockfile's token or an approver token — gets `AccessRefused`.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`AccessRefused`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#accessrefused) when this connection does not stand as `window` · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `set_plugin_enabled`, scope `session`, area `plugins`; igni answers with `message`.

**Example**

```python
info = await session.plugins.set_enabled(name="acme-review", enabled=False)
print(info.text)
```

## igni.marketplaces.add()

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`AccessRefused`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#accessrefused) when this connection does not stand as `window` · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

## igni.marketplaces.list()


## igni.marketplaces.refresh()

Fetch marketplaces' catalogues again.

```python
async def refresh(self, name: str | None = None) -> InfoMessage
```

`name` is one marketplace; absent or empty refreshes every one.
Returns an `info` message, sent in place of an `rpc_response`,
whose text says what was refreshed, or why not.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str \| None` | `None` | The marketplace to refresh; every marketplace when absent. |

**Returns** [`InfoMessage`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/events-reference#infomessage).

**How long** `long` — Runs something that takes as long as it takes: a git clone, the agent, a shell command, a model summarising.
The client waits up to 600 seconds.

**Access** [`client`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — any connection igni admitted.

**On the wire** RPC method `refresh_marketplaces`, scope `igni`, area `plugins`; igni answers with `message`.

**Example**

